t: A 32-bit microcontroller family that powers retro BASIC computers and USB gadgets.
steps: Buy a ready-made board such as the chipKIT Fubarino Mini, an Olimex DuinoMite, or the Olimex PIC32-RETROBSD.
Install the free Arduino IDE on your computer.
Add the chipKIT core through the Boards Manager.
Pick your board and plug it in with a USB cable.
Open the Blink example and upload it.
Watch the onboard LED blink, then change the timing.
Try a DuinoMite next for a BASIC computer with a screen and keyboard.
meta: Open Board. From $28.68. A few stores.
